text:
support-alex: Heads up — PaperCo (tenant_paperco) opened a ticket (7821). Their dashboard heatmap shows a zeroed 6-hour window (2026-03-17 02:00–08:00 UTC) for usage and hourly counts. Screenshot attached. Can someone take a look? :eyes:

devon: On it. Any recent ETL/consumer restarts or deploys in that window? Also paste the console query that returns zeros (or an API curl).

support-alex: We saw an ETL worker restart around 03:15 UTC. Quick API sample: 
```
curl -s "https://internal-metrics.svc/usage?tenant=tenant_paperco&start=2026-03-17T02:00Z&end=2026-03-17T08:00Z" | jq .
[]
```
No rows returned.

maria-l: Likely ingestion/connector gap or consumer offset problem. Can we check kafka consumer lag and the sink connector logs for that tenant? Run the consumer-lag script: 
```
./tools/kafka-consumer-lag --group etl-usage-consumer --topic usage-rollup --tenant tenant_paperco
```

sre-jen: I see an automated restart for etl-worker-7 at 2026-03-17T03:15:12Z — pod restartCount=1, reason=OOMKilled in kube events. Log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-17T03:14:58Z ERROR out-of-memory: process killed
2026-03-17T03:15:12Z INFO starting etl-worker v2.4.1
```
Also got an alert: autoscaler scaled etl-workers from 3->5 at 03:20 due to backlog.

etl-bot: ALERT: consumer-lag(etl-usage-consumer) > 1500 for tenant_paperco between 03:00-03:25 UTC. scale-up triggered.

devon: Ok — two action items: (1) try a targeted replay for the missing window so console shows numbers again, (2) investigate why the sink connector/consumer dropped messages during the restart. Run the replay script for that tenant/time slice and paste the job id here: 
```
./scripts/replay.sh --start 2026-03-17T02:00Z --end 2026-03-17T08:00Z --tenant tenant_paperco
```

support-alex: Ran the replay command, output: 
```
Enqueued replay job id=jr_92031 for tenant_paperco
Partitions scheduled: 12
Failed partitions: 1 -> error: "offset already committed / duplicate-message-handling"
```
So most partitions queued, one partition errored.

maria-l: That duplicate/offset error smells like a TTL/deduplication mismatch in the rollup writer. We've seen truncation flags and dedupe toggles cause suppressed writes if offsets are interpreted as already committed. Can you run a raw ingest count for tenant on the raw events table for the window to verify data existed? 
```
SELECT count(*) FROM raw_ingest.events WHERE tenant_id='tenant_paperco' AND ts >= '2026-03-17T02:00:00Z' AND ts < '2026-03-17T08:00:00Z';
```

sre-jen: Ran that query — raw_ingest has ~14.2k rows for that tenant in the window. So data arrived. But the sink connector logs show no publishes to rollup topic between 02:05–03:30 for partition 7. Also found a config flip in last deploy: `truncate_write=true` was enabled in the rollup writer config (commit 7f3b9c) which can drop messages when combined with dedupe logic. I can revert that flag on staging and run a quick smoke.

devon: If truncate_write=true caused dropped writes, revert to false and deploy a small patch to dedicated rollup writer. Then re-run replay for the failed partition(s). Also add a temporary console fallback to display last-known-good numbers while backfill runs. Proposed ETA: revert + deploy in 30–40m, targeted backfill 60–90m after that.

support-alex: Noted. I'll message PaperCo with an ETA ~2 hours and that we have enqueued a backfill and are rolling back a config change.

maria-l: For the failed partition, run the replay with --force-offset-reset for that partition after the revert. Example: 
```
./scripts/replay.sh --job jr_92031 --force-offset-reset --partitions 7
```

etl-bot: INFO: replay job jr_92031 status=ENQUEUED partitions=11 failed=1

sre-jen: I'm starting the revert in canary now (rolling 1 pod). Will monitor sink connector logs to confirm publishes resume.

devon: Thanks — once publishes resume and backfill finishes, update this thread and support-alex can inform the customer. Also add a small postmortem note with root cause: truncate_write flag + restart race causing sink skip.

support-alex: Customer updated. They'll wait for confirmation. Will follow up when backfill completes. :thumbsup:
